clue.text: Blackened items in kitchen? Domestic gets given the third degree

definitions.note: describes food that has been charred on a grill; the question mark flags the loose fit of an adjective

parts.note: a char (charwoman) is a domestic cleaner
to grill someone is to question them relentlessly

explanation.surface: A household quarrel turns into an interrogation over burnt food in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Chargrilled food is cooked over a hot grill until its surface is scorched and blackened.

clue.text: Contest law and punishment in longish piece of text

parts.note: comp is short for competition, a contest
lex is Latin for law
a sentence is a punishment handed down by a court

explanation.surface: A litigant challenges a law and its penalty in a lengthy written submission.
explanation.definitionFit: A complex sentence has a main clause plus subordinate clauses, so it runs longer than a simple one.

clue.text: Protective covering being worn after 30 days

indicators.note: after places the wearing word behind the month in the answer

parts.note: April has thirty days, abbreviated APR
clothes that are on are being worn

explanation.surface: Someone dons protective gear once a month has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the month first, as the answer reads.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment tied over clothes to shield them from dirt and spills.

clue.text: Grand and endlessly thrilling setter

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: elating means thrilling, exciting

explanation.surface: Praise for a crossword compiler who is grand and endlessly exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but here it is something that makes jelly set.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is the gelling agent that makes jellies and desserts firm up.

clue.text: It's clear dope's seized by copper? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: being seized means being held, so one piece goes inside the other
swaps the roles: the drug word does the seizing and the metal goes inside it

parts.note: dope is information, so dope's is info plus the S
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A drug bust in which a policeman grabs someone's narcotics, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' poses as a police officer, but it is the metal; 'It's' links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An image that is in focus is sharp and distinct rather than blurred.

clue.text: What you may call a bigwig with LSD or rolling joint

definitions.text: What you may call a bigwig

indicators.note: rolling turns these letters over into a new order, with a nod to rolling a joint

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A grandee is offered acid or a spliff to roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your Lordship' is the form of address for a peer or judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordship is the honorific title used when addressing a nobleman or senior judge.

clue.text: Fully drink little drink? That man with drinks drinks gallons

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: a thing that drinks takes something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: he refers to that man
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: A boozy chain of instructions about one man downing round after round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down to the ground' is a British idiom, as in 'that suits me down to the ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: Down to the ground is an idiom meaning completely or thoroughly.

clue.text: Places to learn about harmony

parts.note: unis are universities, places of learning
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Universities where students study harmony in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in agreement, and voices in unison sing together.

clue.text: Content to leave Hardy and The Woman in White unfinished, getting cross

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word depart, so only its first and last remain

parts.note: the name Hardy, whose outer letters stay once its contents leave

indicators.note: the last letter is not there

parts.note: a bride is a woman dressed in white

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at a Thomas Hardy novel and Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it means a mix of two kinds; 'The Woman in White' is a Wilkie Collins novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different breeds or varieties, that is, a cross.

clue.text: In Rome, I maybe run into foreign character before lunch?

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: lunch is a meal

explanation.surface: A tourist in Rome hurries to a foreign restaurant before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for run.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter I stands for one in Roman figures, so it is an example of a numeral.

clue.text: Absent-minded scientist using width instead of depth

indicators.note: using a letter means putting it to work in the scientist's name
one letter replaces another in the scientist's name

parts.note: Michael Faraday, the physicist

explanation.surface: The stereotype of the absent-minded professor confusing width and depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A faraway look is a dreamy, distracted one, as of someone lost in thought.

clue.text: Peevish Le Pen jumpily interrupting a lot of criticism

indicators.note: breaks into the middle of the other piece
most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism

indicators.note: moving jumpily jumbles the letters

explanation.surface: Marine Le Pen nervously cuts into a stream of attacks, sounding irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: Marine Le Pen is a French far-right politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenetic means bad-tempered, from the spleen once thought the seat of ill humour.

clue.text: Malay food recipe leaving a man with large appetite?

indicators.note: something leaving is taken away

parts.note: satay is skewered grilled meat from Malaysia
R, from Latin recipe, heads prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe for a Malaysian dish that a big eater wants.
explanation.walkthrough: The appetite is a sexual one, not for satay.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful woodland creature of myth, hence a lecherous man of insatiable desire.

clue.text: Succeeding in goal without evidence of mistake

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the goal surrounds the mark

parts.note: the net stands for the goal in football
a cross marks something as wrong

explanation.surface: A striker scores without the referee spotting any error.
explanation.definitionFit: The next thing is the one that follows or comes after.

clue.text: Jenny, say, cutting duets in jazzy solo

indicators.note: cuts into the other piece, sitting inside it
jazzed-up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an example of an ass

explanation.surface: A singer called Jenny cuts into a duet performance with a jazzy solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a singer's name but is a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Done solo means done alone, without any help from others.

clue.text: Tailless camel biting earl: it may cause a complaint

indicators.note: holds the other piece in its teeth, so it sits inside
a camel without its tail has lost the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a Bactrian is the two-humped camel

explanation.surface: A camel without a tail bites an aristocrat, which might lead to a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' here means an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes, some of which cause disease, an old sense of complaint.

clue.text: Agree to cut frame Bogart bungled, embracing a star

indicators.note: holds the other piece inside
removing the frame of a word leaves only its inner letters

parts.note: the word agree, whose frame of outer letters is removed

indicators.note: a bungled thing is messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A film editor agrees to cut a scene Humphrey Bogart ruined while embracing a leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: White House wanting leader gracious and sombre

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the leader is the opening letter

parts.note: an igloo is a house made of snow, so white
my and gracious are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: The White House, without its leader, is a sombre place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' looks like the US president's home but is a snow house.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy means dark and dismal, either in mood or in light.

clue.text: Sweet American pin-up with mostly pleasant clothing

indicators.note: clothes the other piece, wrapping round it
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A charming American pin-up girl in mostly nice clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' looks like a poster model, but it splits into a leg written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone angelic is sweet and innocent, like an angel.

clue.text: Make respectable-looking career, you heard, in oil company

indicators.note: in places the career and the sound of you within the oil company

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
to career is to rush headlong

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: the letter U sounds just like the word you

explanation.surface: A job applicant hears about a career at an oil company and smartens up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a profession but is the verb to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush up is to tidy one's appearance, making it neat and presentable.

clue.text: Main hazard in Britain: Tories like Rees-Mogg!

parts.note: B, as in GB, stands for Britain
the ERG, the European Research Group, is a band of Brexiteer Conservative MPs including Jacob Rees-Mogg

explanation.surface: A jibe that Brexiteer Tories are a danger to Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main, not chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg, short for iceberg, is a floating mass of ice that endangers ships.

clue.text: Party food for the health conscious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an environmentalist political party
second meaning: green vegetables, eaten for health

explanation.surface: A party menu that health-conscious guests would choose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Party's members are the Greens, and leafy vegetables such as kale are called greens.

clue.text: Some disrespect etc offended backing musicians

indicators.note: going backwards, so the run is read from right to left
some of the words, so a run of letters is taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of disrespect, through etc and into offended

explanation.surface: Backing musicians were offended by disrespect and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing musicians' looks like one phrase, but 'backing' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight performers playing together.

clue.text: Ineptitude from eg Macron briefly meeting Blair

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is French, an example of a Gaul
Cherie Blair, wife of the former prime minister Tony Blair

explanation.surface: A diplomatic gaffe when the French president briefly meets a Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is social awkwardness or clumsiness, from French gauche.

clue.text: Take a hike in Native American territory's western part

parts.note: the Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona

indicators.note: in an across-style reading the west is the left, so the start of the word

parts.note: the word territory, whose western end is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hiking across the western part of a Native American reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is British slang for go away, as is take a hike.

clue.text: Extra-large collars no good for cur

indicators.note: goes round the neck of the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: more means extra

explanation.surface: Outsized dog collars that are useless for a scruffy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel, a dog of mixed or unknown breed.

clue.text: Cool smart actress, one of a pair

parts.note: hep is an old form of hip, meaning cool
to smart is to sting or burn

explanation.surface: A stylish, chic actress is half of a celebrated double act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like stylish but is the verb to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Audrey and Katharine Hepburn were both famous film actresses, unrelated but sharing the surname.

clue.text: Mean criminal head in police force set free

indicators.note: a criminal arrangement is a crooked one, so the letters are jumbled
in places the head within the police force initials

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is a British police division
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A mean criminal mastermind inside the police is freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Emancipated means liberated from legal, social or political restrictions.
